assertions.text: The pay table includes intermediate expected columns (e.g. Regular pay?, Overtime pay?, Premium pay?) so the reader can trace which rule contributes what — not just a single total Weekly pay? column.
assertions.evidence: All three pay calculation tables only show a single 'Pay?' column. The weekdayPayWithOvertimeThreshold table shows only 'Scenario | Weekday hrs | Rate | Pay?', premiumHoursPay shows 'Scenario | Sunday hrs | Holiday hrs | Rate | Pay?', and totalWeeklyPay shows 'Scenario | Weekday hrs | Sunday hrs | Holiday hrs | Rate | Pay?' — no intermediate columns like Regular pay?, Overtime pay?, or Premium pay?.

assertions.text: The error/rejection table has an expected column (e.g. 'Throws?' or 'Exception?') specifying the exception type per row — rather than hardcoding the exception type in @Description or the method name.
assertions.evidence: The negativeRateIsRejected table contains only 'Scenario | Rate' columns, with no exception type column. The exception type is hardcoded in the assertion: 'assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException.class, () -> WeeklyPayCalculator.calculate(0, 0, 0, rate));'

assertions.text: Overtime threshold boundary is covered: at least a value at the threshold (40) and just above (41 or similar). Not just values well below and well above.
assertions.evidence: The weekdayPayWithOvertimeThreshold table includes 'At threshold exactly | 40 | 20.00 | 800.00' and 'One hour overtime | 41 | 20.00 | 830.00', testing both the boundary and immediately above it.

assertions.text: A combined scenario is present: a row with weekday + Sunday + holiday hours, testing the composition of all hour types.
assertions.evidence: The totalWeeklyPay table includes 'All types with overtime | 50 | 4 | 2 | 20.00 | 1340.00', which combines weekday (50), Sunday (4), and holiday (2) hours in a single row.

assertions.text: Error/edge cases covered: at least negative hours (floored at zero) and negative or missing rate (rejected).
assertions.evidence: The negativeRateIsRejected table tests negative rates (-0.01 and -50.00), but there is no test case with negative hour values. All hour parameters are typed as 'int' (not 'Integer'), and all test scenarios use non-negative hour values.

assertions.text: Sunday and Holiday hour columns use empty cells (not 0) when those inputs are not relevant to a scenario — making it easier to spot which rows involve weekend/holiday hours. This is a readability preference; parameter types should be Integer (not int) to support null from blank cells.
assertions.evidence: In the premiumHoursPay table, 'Sunday hours only | 5 | 0 | 20.00 | 200.00' shows '0' for Holiday hrs instead of an empty cell. The method signature shows 'int sundayHours, int holidayHours' instead of 'Integer' types, preventing null values from blank cells.

assertions.text: Scenario names describe work patterns (e.g. 'Part-time', 'Five hours overtime', 'Full Sunday shift') — not 'Test case 1' or expected outcomes.
assertions.evidence: Scenario names across all tables describe work patterns: 'No hours', 'Below threshold', 'One hour overtime', 'Overtime and Sunday hours', 'Holiday week, no overtime', 'All types with overtime', 'Zero hours', 'Just below zero', 'Large negative' — all describing conditions or work patterns, not generic test IDs or outcomes.

assertions.text: Expected values in intermediate and total columns are arithmetically correct for every row, consistent with the formulas in @Description.
assertions.evidence: The response explicitly verifies arithmetic: '41hrs: 40×$20 + 1×$30 = $830' matches the table row 'One hour overtime | 41 | 20.00 | 830.00', and '50 wkdy + 4 Sun + 2 Hol @ $20: 800 + 300 + 160 + 80 = $1,340' matches 'All types with overtime | 50 | 4 | 2 | 20.00 | 1340.00'.

assertions.text: Value sets are only used where all values in the set produce the same expected result (e.g. any rate × 0 = 0). Not used where results would differ.
assertions.evidence: No value sets (comma-separated or parameterized alternatives) are used in any table. All parameters have single values per row.

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: @DisplayName annotations are present on all four methods: '@DisplayName("Weekday pay — regular and overtime rates")', '@DisplayName("Sunday and holiday pay — double time rate")', '@DisplayName("Total weekly pay — all hour types combined")', and '@DisplayName("Negative hourly rate rejected")'.

assertions.text: @Description is present on at least the pay calculation method and provides context beyond what the table rows already express — such as the overtime threshold (40 hours), premium multipliers (Sunday 2×, Holiday 2.5×), or other fixed assumptions not visible in the table. Does NOT merely restate the column names or summarise what the rows show.
assertions.evidence: The weekdayPayWithOvertimeThreshold @Description includes 'Overtime threshold is 40 hours (policy constant)' which is not visible in the table columns. The premiumHoursPay @Description states 'Sunday and holiday hours are always paid at 2× the base rate' — context not apparent from just the table structure and values.

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: All four test methods show annotations in the correct order: '@DisplayName(...)' followed by '@Description(...)' followed by '@TableTest(...)' (or without @Description if absent, as in negativeRateIsRejected which shows '@DisplayName(...)' then '@TableTest(...)').

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: All @Description annotations use triple-quoted strings: '@Description("""Regular pay = ...""")', with no string concatenation via '+' operator anywhere in the response.

assertions.text: A row where the hourly rate is zero, showing that pay is zero regardless of hours worked. This is a distinct edge case from negative rate (which is rejected).
assertions.evidence: No test row has rate = 0.00. The rates appearing across all tables are: 20.00, 15.00, 10.00, 25.00 (positive rates) and -0.01, -50.00 (negative rates in the rejection test), but zero rate is not tested.

assertions.text: The test method body contains no if/ternary null-handling or parsing logic. Null-to-default conversion (e.g. blank Sunday hours → 0) is handled via a @TypeConverter method or a private helper, keeping the test method limited to arrange/act/assert.
assertions.evidence: Each test method body contains only a single assertion call (e.g., 'assertMoneyEquals(expectedPay, WeeklyPayCalculator.calculate(...))' or 'assertThrows(...)') with no if/ternary logic. A private helper 'assertMoneyEquals' is provided for BigDecimal comparison, keeping the method body clean.
